$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Microsoft Foundry hub pages (Agents, Content filters, Evaluations, Prompt flow, Fine-tuning, Custom models). Proven by tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py.

azure.foundry.agents.title: Foundry Agents (Assistants API: agents, threads, runs, code interpreter, file search, vector stores)
limitations: Agents are Assistants API assistants over a model deployment (the small local model, so quality is toy-grade). Runs execute synchronously inside the create call. Tools: function calling (submit_tool_outputs), code_interpreter (real Python in a restricted sandbox, not a VM: input files from tool_resources, stdout in run steps, written files saved with file_path annotations, no image output) and file_search (real retrieval over vector stores: files are parsed, chunked and embedded with the local embedding model and ranked by exact cosine; answers carry file_citation annotations). Not available: Bing grounding, Azure AI Search, OpenAPI, Logic Apps, Azure Functions and MCP tools, expiry policies, a chunking_strategy other than the default, and file_search ranking options. State is process-local. Served at both `/openai/*` (every verb: GET/POST/DELETE) and the Foundry project endpoint `/api/projects/<project>/` (azure-ai-agents 1.1.0 AgentsClient: assistants, threads, messages, runs, run steps, files, vector stores, vector store files and batches; run steps include the file_search tool_calls step).

azure.foundry.content-filters.title: Content filters (raiPolicies enforced on deployments)
limitations: A custom content filter is enforced on every deployment that names it, through the Bedrock Guardrails content engine (keyword and local-embedding scoring), so detection is toy-grade rather than Microsoft's classifiers. Hate, Sexual, Violence and Jailbreak map to the engine; SelfHarm is not modelled, and Microsoft's built-in default policies never block.

azure.foundry.evaluations.title: Evaluations (Azure OpenAI Evals API)
limitations: The Azure OpenAI Evals API (openai SDK client.evals: evals, runs, output_items) runs for real with string_check, text_similarity, label_model and score_model graders. Model graders are judged by the small local model, so scores are indicative and will not match Azure's. Python graders, the logs and stored_completions sources, and gleu and meteor are rejected; run state is process-local.

azure.foundry.promptflow.title: Prompt flow (flow.dag.yaml)
limitations: A flow.dag.yaml with inputs, outputs, llm and prompt nodes is converted to the Bedrock Flows runner and run on the local model (Vyomi extension at /openai/vyomi/promptflow). Python tool nodes and other node types of the Prompt flow SDK are rejected, flow state is in memory, and there is no compute session or managed online endpoint.

azure.foundry.finetuning.title: Fine-tuning (Azure OpenAI fine_tuning/jobs)
limitations: On the trainable bases (the embedding model or vyomi.head.*) a job really trains a small classifier, router or reranker head, capped at 2000 rows, 5 MB and 20 labels; it is not a language model. On every other base model a job completes with a fine-tuned model record only: nothing is trained.

azure.foundry.custom-models.title: Custom models (import a LoRA adapter, Vyomi extension)
limitations: Azure has no API that registers a custom LoRA adapter, so POST /openai/vyomi/custom-models is a Vyomi extension. The model is a SmolLM2 135M or 360M base plus your GGUF adapter (up to 50 MB), deployed through a normal ARM deployment (format Vyomi) and called with chat/completions. Serving needs the Nano console tab (llama.cpp WASM, base downloaded from Hugging Face on first use); Mesh and offline store the import but cannot serve it yet.

azure.foundry.project-endpoint.title: Foundry project endpoint (azure-ai-projects: agents v2 + versions, Responses with agent_reference, conversations, connections, deployments)
limitations: `<host>/api/projects/<project>` is served by the same Assistants/Responses core (no new backend). Verified with azure-ai-projects 2.11.0 AIProjectClient: connections.list/get/get_default (derived from the ARM Cognitive Services accounts and Search services; keys are placeholders), deployments.list/get (from ARM deployments), agents.create_version/get/list/list_versions/get_version/delete_version/delete (prompt agents; the definition is stored), get_openai_client() responses.create(conversation=..., extra_body={agent_reference}) which applies the agent's model, instructions and function tools, and conversations create/retrieve/delete + items create/list. NOT modelled: hosted/workflow agents, agent tools other than function calling (Bing, Azure AI Search, MCP, code interpreter in v2), datasets/indexes/evaluators/red teams (listings return empty), memory stores, telemetry. The SDK's BearerTokenCredentialPolicy refuses non-TLS endpoints, so a local plain-http endpoint needs a custom authentication_policy that adds the Authorization header (the simulator requires a bearer or api-key header). State is process-local.

azure.foundry.on-your-data.title: Azure OpenAI On Your Data (chat completions grounded on an AI Search index: data_sources[azure_search])
limitations: chat/completions with extra_body.data_sources of type azure_search retrieves from the simulator's own AI Search index (same engine as the native search data plane; api_key / access_token / managed-identity auth values are accepted, only api_key is checked; endpoint forms: /azure-data/search/<service>, the ARM-extension path, <service>.search.* host, or the root when one service exists) and returns message.context {citations[{content,title,url,filepath,chunk_id}], intent} with [docN] markers; stream=true sends the context in the first delta. top_n_documents, filter, fields_mapping (content/title/url/filepath), in_scope and query_type simple/semantic/vector/vector_simple_hybrid/vector_semantic_hybrid work best-effort on the existing engine (vector query embeds the question with the local embedding model). strictness is accepted but not applied, citations carry no rerank_score and the intent is the user question verbatim (no query rewrite). Answer quality is the small local model's. Other data source types (cosmos_db, elasticsearch, azure_ml_index, mongo_db, pinecone) are rejected with 400 BadRequest. The same shared core serves Nano; it answers only while a WebLLM model is loaded (otherwise the native 503), and the Nano path was not separately browser-tested.
